newsitem.title: CHINA: FORECAST - China savings seen up 28 pct in Q2.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - China savings seen up 28 pct in Q2.

text.p: China's personal savings are expected to rise 28 percent in the second quarter over a year ago, the China News Service said on Monday.
It quoted the State Information Centre of the State Economic and Trade Commission as saying that bank loans in the second quarter would rise 21.5 percent.

Personal savings rose to 4.2 trillion yuan ($506 billion) in the first four months of the year, up 24 percent from the same period in 1996. Bank loans in the first four months reached 200 billion yuan for a rise of 20 percent over last year.
Retail sales in the second quarter would reach 657.6 billion yuan, representing a rise of 15 percent over the year-ago period, it said.
Retail sales in the first quarter totalled 663.3 billion yuan, up by 15.5 percent over the year-ago period.
Industrial output was forecast to rise 15.8 percent in the second quarter, with output of state-owned industries climbing 7.8 percent compared with the year-ago period, it said.
Industrial output during the first quarter rose 11 percent year on year to 452.5 billion yuan, according to the State Statistical Bureau.
